summary: Count out loud (or sign) by ones to at least 20.
See how many at a glance, up to 5, without counting, and say the number.
Count objects up to 10, one number word for each object, in order.
Answer "How many?" with the last number counted, up to about 10.
Count up to 5 scattered objects, or count 5 out of a bigger pile.
Know each next number when counting means one more.
Tell if one group has more than, less than or the same as another, up to 5.
Use order words, first to fifth, to say where something is in a line.
Match a group of objects to its written number, 0 to 5.
Recognize the numbers to 10 and, with help, write some of them.
Show adding and taking away with fingers, objects or drawings.
Solve simple add and take-away stories, adding or taking up to 5, within 10.
With help, start counting on from the bigger number to add 1 or 2.
Fill in what's missing in a simple pattern.
Copy a simple pattern somewhere new and make it longer.
Find the part that repeats in a pattern, like red-blue in red-blue-red-blue.
Use compare words like shortest, heavier, biggest or later.
Compare or put in order up to 5 objects by height, weight or another measure.
Measure with the same unit over and over, like a line of snap cubes.
Name shapes and describe them by their sides and corners.
Name circles, squares, rectangles and triangles of any size or turn.
Compare and sort flat and solid shapes of different sizes, and say how they differ.
Put simple shapes together to make bigger shapes.
Use position words like up, down, in front of and behind.
Follow directions about moving their own body, like "Stand up" or "Move forward."
